raw_response:
I farm in Quzhou County, so I would stay with the crop pattern I know best and trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize. At my age, I would not take on a complicated mix of cash crops. Wheat and maize fit my land, fit the local weather, fit the machines people around me use, and give me the safest balance between grain for sale and manageable field work. I would use improved seed, not the most expensive risky option, because I want stable yield more than chasing the top result. I would keep fertilizer at a moderate level, give water at the key stages, and spray only as needed to control the main diseases, weeds, and insects. For tillage, I would keep it simple: rotary tillage for maize after wheat, and rotary tillage again before wheat sowing, because it is easier for me to manage than deep ploughing every season and more reliable than full no-tillage on my farm. My whole plan is to keep costs controlled, avoid overwork, and make sure I get a dependable harvest from the land this year.
